description: Versioned allow/block corpus for the plan-c21cdc secret guard (D18/RISK-16). Every token-shaped string here is stored ONLY as inert fragments and a reconstruction recipe: no committed line contains a complete provider-token signature, so this fixture cannot itself trip repository push protection. The test in ReviewRunArtifacts.Tests.ps1 assembles each `segments` list at runtime (concatenating `literal` fragments and `repeat`/`cycle` bodies) and asserts the guard blocks every `expected: block` case and passes every `expected: allow` case. `block` cases are synthetic — low-entropy bodies that match the shape but are not real credentials; `allow` cases are values that share a high-confidence shape yet are known non-secrets (redacted, masked, documented examples) plus ordinary tokenlike strings the guard must not flag.
reconstruction: A case's value is the ordered concatenation of its `segments`. A segment is `{"literal": "..."}` (used verbatim), `{"repeat": "X", "count": n}` (the character repeated n times) or `{"cycle": "abc", "count": n}` (the alphabet cycled to length n). No segment holds a complete token prefix plus body together.

cases.why: A classic GitHub personal access token shape: gh + p_ + 36 base62.
The gho_ OAuth variant of the same family.
The fine-grained github_pat_ prefix plus a long alphanumeric body.
An AWS access key id: AKIA + 16 uppercase/digits.
A Google API key: AIza + 35 url-safe characters.
A Slack bot token: xoxb- plus a long body.
A Stripe live secret key: sk_live_ plus a long body.
An npm token: npm_ plus 36 base62.
A PEM private-key banner. The banner alone is inert — no key material is committed — but it is a high-confidence marker the guard must catch.
The AWS documentation example key. It matches the AKIA shape but is a published non-secret the guard must not block.
A token a reviewer already redacted: matches the gh shape but its body is the REDACTED marker, so the guard must pass it (it is not a live credential).
A masked value: matches the shape but the body is a run of X's, which is a mask rather than a secret.
A content digest. It is long and token-shaped but matches no credential family, so the guard must not flag it — the review artifacts are full of these.
A run id. Token-shaped but not a credential.
An ordinary reviewer reference. The common case the guard must never false-positive on.
